paper.title: SceneBot: Contact-Prompted General Humanoid Whole Body Tracking with Scene-Interaction
paper.source_version: arXiv v1, submitted 2026-06-25; official demo/runtime repository commit 430c29c1801aceb813506d86f3a8cffeba250df3, checked 2026-08-30

decision_relevance.why_admitted: SceneBot makes contact intent an explicit, timed reference channel and reports reward/contact ablations on unseen motions, directly informing oracle-manifest design and a carefully bounded task-reward hypothesis while exposing strict fixed-controller and fixed-tracking-reward compatibility conditions.
not_evidence_for: A harness-only gain when the frozen controller does not already consume per-link contact labels
An autonomous high-level oracle or contact-schedule planner
A task-reward-only improvement under an otherwise identical policy and observation contract
Permission to edit contact-tracking terms when Sam's tracking reward is frozen
Changing scene assets inside Sam's initial fixed-scene experiment
Object-instance-resolved contact plans in multi-object scenes
Broad real-world reliability or statistical uncertainty across training seeds
Availability of the paper's PPO training, hindsight reconstruction code, or released training dataset

mechanisms.name: Contact-prompted whole-body tracker
mechanisms.description: A single PPO policy consumes a kinematic reference, robot-link × scene-type contact labels, proprioception, and global root state to track free-space, terrain, object, and sitting motions.

mechanisms.name: Temporal robot-scene interaction graph
mechanisms.description: Temporal edges connect five robot key links to terrain or object nodes at contact locations; candidates derive from low relative velocity/acceleration and are pruned for off-interval collision or force-closure infeasibility.

mechanisms.name: Hindsight scene reconstruction
mechanisms.description: Retargeted human motion and the interaction graph generate 2.5D terrain plateaus plus plate-based object geometry and trajectories that are consistent with inferred contacts.

mechanisms.name: Asymmetric correctness and duration reward
mechanisms.description: Desired active contacts receive correctness credit; cumulative contact duration is rewarded only up to 0.5 seconds, with a mismatch termination and separate non-ankle/non-wrist contact penalty.

mechanisms.name: LiDAR-IMU global root estimation
mechanisms.description: SuperOdometry supplies global motion while a pelvis IMU supplies pitch/roll and yaw-rate fusion at 200 Hz, mitigating scene-reference drift.

failure_modes.name: Retargeting artifacts corrupt inferred contact
failure_modes.description: Foot sliding and other low-fidelity retargeting artifacts remove the physical cues required for stable scene-interaction graph construction.

failure_modes.name: Nonphysical source-motion failure
failure_modes.description: Motion recovered from video or generated by a model may lack physical consistency and destabilize graph construction.

failure_modes.name: Under-specified reconstruction thresholds
failure_modes.description: v1 does not numerically specify low-velocity/acceleration contact thresholds, temporal consistency windows, plateau-merging tolerances, force-closure tests, or the contact-mismatch timeout.

failure_modes.name: Heuristic object-stabilization dependency
failure_modes.description: Some reconstructed objects do not begin in a resting pose, so training applies a stabilizing force until force-closure grasp; this changes dynamics and may mask grasp failures.

failure_modes.name: No autonomous contact-schedule oracle
failure_modes.description: The low-level policy requires an external high-level decision maker to supply contact commands; autonomous perceptive control remains future work.

failure_modes.name: Scene-type labels omit object identity
failure_modes.description: Contact labels encode robot link × terrain/object type, not a specific object instance or desired contact pose; multi-object disambiguation is outside the reported interface.

failure_modes.name: Contact channel and scene generation can violate the fixed contract
failure_modes.description: Adding contact observations changes a non-contact controller, while reconstructing scene assets changes the fixed scene; neither is a harness-only intervention unless admitted before freezing the MDP.

failure_modes.name: Evaluation uncertainty gap
failure_modes.description: The paper gives exact point estimates and 20 unseen sequences per category but no independent training seeds, confidence intervals, or variance; the hardware state-estimation result covers 10 trials of one scenario.

failure_modes.name: Training and reconstruction release gap
failure_modes.description: The official page marks code/data coming soon; the public pinned repository contains a browser deployment runtime and compiled policy assets but not the reported PPO training, scene reconstruction pipeline, or released training corpus.

evaluation.name: Unseen-motion MuJoCo sim-to-sim protocol
evaluation.description: Twenty unseen motion sequences with reconstructed scenes are evaluated in each of four categories using joint error, global root errors, and task-specific binary success.

evaluation.name: SceneBot versus SONIC
evaluation.description: SceneBot and SONIC both achieve 100% free-space success, while SceneBot reports 95/100/100% on object/terrain/sit versus SONIC's 5/15/0% under the paper's protocol.

evaluation.name: Contact-label ablation
evaluation.description: Training without labels yields 0% object and 60% terrain success; retaining the trained model but disabling foot labels at test gives 85% terrain success.

evaluation.name: Global-state ablation
evaluation.description: Removing global root position and linear velocity reduces object success from 95% to 20% and terrain success from 100% to 45%.

evaluation.name: Reconstruction versus OmniRetarget
evaluation.description: On OMOMO, the paper reports better object-interaction tracking with reconstructed scenes than a tuned scene-aware OmniRetarget baseline, attributing failures to hand-object misalignment and penetration tradeoffs.

evaluation.name: OptiTrack-referenced hardware state estimation
evaluation.description: Ten box-pickup-and-stage trials report 0.032 m root-position, 0.018 rad orientation, and 0.092 m/s velocity error with 80% task success.

evidence.claim: arXiv v1 was submitted 25 June 2026 with the stated title and six authors.
SceneBot gives a low-level general tracker both reference motion and robot-side per-link contact labels; a high-level decision maker must supply the extra contact command.
Five key robot links, two scene types, temporal candidate/pruning rules, and graph-conditioned terrain/object reconstruction define the hindsight data engine.

The PPO policy consumes a 93-D reference command and contact labels; contact correctness is asymmetric, duration clips at 0.5 s, and object training uses mismatch termination plus a stabilizing force.
Table 2 reports all tracking/contact reward equations, weights, penalties, kernel scales, and the 1 N undesired-contact threshold.
Training uses 7.5 hours of data; Figure 5 reports 974 object, 783 flat-terrain, 297 terrain, and 38 sitting clips.
The MuJoCo sim-to-sim protocol evaluates 20 unseen motion sequences and reconstructed scenes in each of four categories against SONIC and three ablations.
Table 3 reports exact joint, root-position, root-orientation, and success metrics for SceneBot, SONIC, and all listed ablations.
Global-root and contact-label ablations identify drift, grasp, and frequent contact-switch failures; test-time foot-label removal retains 85% terrain success.
On OMOMO, reconstructed assets outperform tuned OmniRetarget assets; the paper attributes the gap to alignment/penetration tradeoffs and grasp failure.
The 200 Hz SuperOdometry/pelvis-IMU pipeline reports 0.032 m, 0.018 rad, and 0.092 m/s mean errors plus 80% success over 10 hardware experiments.
Scene reconstruction requires high-fidelity retargeting and is vulnerable to foot sliding and physically inconsistent video/generated motion.
Success is defined separately for terrain, object, sitting, and free-space tasks using falls, root-height error, grasp retention, and pelvis-chair contact.
An autonomous perceptive high-level controller is stated as future work.
The official page marks Data and Code as Coming Soon while separately exposing an interactive demo.
